title: Mixed Tin-Lead Perovskite Near-Infrared Photodetectors: Stability Challenges and Engineering Strategies
content: Mixed tin-lead (Sn-Pb) halide perovskites are promising absorbers for near-infrared (NIR) photo-detection because of their tunable narrow bandgaps, strong optical absorption, and compatibility with low-temperature solution processing. However, mismatched crystallization kinetics of Sn- and Pb-containing precursors, the oxidation susceptibility of Sn(II), and chemically reactive interfaces can compromise film quality and device stability. This review outlines the electronic structure, carrier dynamics, and defect chemistry of mixed Sn-Pb perovskites, and examines how crystallization control, additive and compositional engineering, and oxidation suppression affect absorber properties. Device-level strategies, including charge-selective contacts, interfacial modification, electrode protection, and encapsulation, are evaluated in relation to charge collection and device degradation. Reported stability results are discussed with attention to testing conditions and the distinction between initial performance and long-term durability. Finally, remaining challenges in linking chemical and structural degradation to electrical performance and improving photodetector reliability are outlined.
